positions.pos: Your answer that control depends on where you start is now one rule everywhere: from satisfied it holds, from neutral it pulls back to dissatisfied, from dissatisfied it holds. So Temper Action from Anger dissatisfied ends at Fear dissatisfied in bars-engine, the ontology game and Sprout. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: The ontology game's routing table (bars-engine content/ontology-game/game.jsx) and the Sprout prototype already said this, noted there as checked against your three stated rules; only wuxing.ts disagreed, lowering satisfied to neutral.

positions.pos: A generative move carries the charge to the next channel on the sheng cycle and raises it one state, and satisfied stays satisfied. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: wuxing.ts, move-engine, the ontology game and the Sprout prototype all do this; only alchemy-graph's growth edges keep the same state.

positions.pos: Following your overrule, Transcend is two steps in one channel: dissatisfied to neutral, then neutral to satisfied. A satisfied channel has no Transcend step. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Your steer on mn-transcend-plus-two: 'The 2 steps makes the most sense'. wuxing.ts already stepped one at a time.

positions.pos: Each face owns the three moves bars-engine's lens-moves already gave it. Two moves have no face yet: Temper Action and Step Through. Daemons own moves too, with no home channel, and their lists come next. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Your answer to mn-q-face-daemon (each face and daemon owns its moves); lens-moves.ts is the only face-to-move map whose ids are all real moves.
